name: Nina Khan
life: “I still remember buying the cheapest roll before a long night on watch.” Friday often includes a stop at Tideline Market, where Nina picks out the bruised fruit first and asks the seller what will ripen by supper.
voice: I buy breakfast on a night wage. I want these new bosses to remember what two coins used to buy.
appearance: On an ordinary day, look for a long navy raincoat and a knotted piece of sail thread on a key ring. Nina has a round face with a pronounced chin, with short black hair swept back. Nina counts on the side of one finger where hardly anybody notices during a conversation.
personality: Nina has excellent recall for voices and a poor memory for official titles. Someone who waited patiently at a counter years ago is more likely to be remembered than the person in charge.
agenda: To preserve a useful two-coin breakfast.
family: Dale Nielsen is Nina’s second cousin. Nina chooses whether to use it. Dale saves a place. The invitation means something because declining it has never ended the friendship between their households. Asked about *A red mitten*, Dale says, “My toddler kept moving it to save a seat for his dad.”
connections: Lee Roche. The quiet loaf specialist meets a regular who counts breakfast in coins.

reactions.situation: The absent owner calls to ask which pastry burned
reactions.response: Nina gives the owner a truthful account without handing back all three workers' decisions.

reactions.situation: A friend asks for a loan due back before payday
reactions.response: Nina agrees on a sum and a date with the friend in private, keeping the arrangement out of family gossip.
